deck: HOW OPERATORS GET LISTED WITH ALE SOLUTIONS, CRS, SEDGWICK, AND THD, AND GET THE FAMILY TO PICK THEIR HOME OVER THE HOTEL
HOW OPERATORS PRICE AGAINST COVERAGE D, CAP UTILITIES IN CONTRACTS, AND HOLD RESERVES BEFORE ARBITRAGING FOR CLAIMS
site_ui.lead: Operators show how displaced families stuck in hotels become multi-month house placements: an $8,100 house replaced a roughly $15,000-a-month hotel bill, and 15 insurance families brought in more than $100K in one month.
site_ui.summary: All 12 chapters synthesize 192 verbatim YouTube practitioner testimonies, from getting booked by insurance relocation companies through leases, lease exits, and insuring the rental operation. Every claim, metric, pro-tip, and operator gate carries timestamped inline attribution to the practitioner who said it.

flow: Submit the home to ALE Solutions, CRS, Sedgwick, and Temporary Housing Directory forms, then confirm each submission by phone within a week because the forms send no confirmation and can create duplicates.

Send weekly or biweekly email blasts to relocation specialists with a PS asking them to forward it and a PPS offering referrals in other cities, and add BNI networking and local fire department outreach.
Ask for the nightly price range instead of the budget, let the agency name a number first, and anchor against the hotel-plus-kennel cost, aiming for about 1.5 to 2x long-term rent.
Write electric and water caps into the agreement and notes, keep cleaning, pet, and deposit fees low enough for the family, and remember the contract is with the agency, not the person.
Run a duplicate 30-day-minimum Airbnb with an open calendar, open the short-stay window no more than 30 days out, and hold a unit 24 hours pending adjuster approval.
Before arbitraging a home for claims, set aside at least six months of reserves, plan three exit strategies, and confirm you can cover net-30 payment terms.
